newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bond prices ended weak but off lows as the market waited for end of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting, and pondered the latest Swiss tender.

The Swiss federal government said early Tuesday it would launch a 4-1/4 percent 20-year bond. Terms of the offer will be announced after auction close on Thursday. Traders were disappointed by the latest tender, which they believed would fail to generate as much demand as an offer for liquid 10- or 11-year paper. The Swiss Treasury sees the issue as a way to get more liquidity in the long end of the yield curve, and also hopes the move will bolster longer swaps.
Some market participants who shorted bonds, hoping these would be reopened in the tender, were also said to have been forced to cover when those bonds were not in the offering.

The short end was bolstered by the strong Swiss franc, now trading at roughly seven-month highs against the mark. The franc's gains have led markets to speculate that the Swiss National Bank will work against the franc's rise with easier interest rates.
On Tuesday morning, SNB operations showed no signs of any move towards an easier policy, traders said.
Prices are compared with Friday's close. Swiss markets were closed on Monday for a holiday.
Euro Swiss francs up three at 98.33.
